analyst_view.overall: Juventus (7th, 18 points, LWLWD) host 19th-placed Venezia (6 points) in Sunday's lunchtime game and need a win after dropping points against lower-table sides. Spalletti returns to a back three of Gatti, Bremer and Lucumi because Kalulu is out and Cambiaso and Celik are still training apart; McKennie and Cabal play wide, Douglas Luiz anchors midfield and Kolo Muani, Alajbegovic and Woltemade are expected up front, with Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Grabara and Nico Gonzalez also out (mostly counted). What changed: the talk of Venezia resting strikers Adams and Yeboah after international trips now comes from one outlet only, while two other line-up guides (one updated Saturday) expect Adams to start with Yeboah or Lauberbach. Venezia play a compact 3-5-2 built for counters, with Franjic and Sverko improving and Adorante still recovering. Referee Alberto Arena's low card record on only three games is already blended in by the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, with Venezia's share only 0.8. Juve are short of their usual wide players (Cambiaso, Celik, Kalulu) against a deep, compact block, which the numbers don't know; the Venezia striker rest I leaned on before is now less likely, with two line-up guides expecting Adams to start, so I soften the lean to about 2.45.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, already raised for Juve's recent corner count (+12%). Venezia defending deep should give Juve plenty of corners, and McKennie and Cabal wide keep that going, but that is what the numbers already show, so I stay at about 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards, cut for both teams' quiet recent run (about -10% and -13%) and for Arena's low record on just three games. Nicola's sides defend aggressively and Venezia are fighting relegation in a game they must make physical, which a three-game referee sample can't capture; a mild lean up to about 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.3 shots, already lifted for Venezia's recent shooting (+18%). Juve will have the ball against a compact block with Kolo Muani, Woltemade and Alajbegovic up front, and Venezia now look likely to start their usual strikers, so I stay at about 30.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target, most of them in Juve's hands (6.0). Juve's expected front three is their usual one and their recent accuracy is already counted, so I stay at about 8.9.
